answer.feedback: Search for a mechanism beyond another static substrate-only growth law. The best-fitting inhibition forms still fail badly: C40/C18 under-predict x2 in E1 around t=2 h and E3 around t=15 h, but over-predict x2 in E2 around t=3 h. This pattern suggests the substrate-consumption dynamics may need a transient or history-dependent component, or a revised substrate balance (for example, variable yield or maintenance), rather than simply a different saturation curve. The supplied summaries do not give the x2 levels at these times, so they do not support labeling these mismatches as high- versus low-substrate; check those regimes against the raw trajectories when proposing the next model.
answer.reasoning: No candidate meets the acceptance rule: every fit has chi2 far above its 95% limit, indicating systematic lack of fit. The highest-weight candidate, C40, also has strongly correlated kinetic parameters and still misses x2 substantially; C18 has essentially the same fit with an additional parameter that runs to an extreme. Relative AIC weight cannot compensate for lack of fit. The data therefore call for another model search, not acceptance or an inconclusive stop.
